thread:
jess_support: Heads-up — ACME (Private/VPC) opened an escalation: TLS handshake failures started immediately after we pushed their cert rotation. Error seen by their services: 'unable to get local issuer certificate'. They say some internal clients succeed and some fail. Sharing notes + reproducer below.

tyler_oncall: Can you paste the exact openssl output you have?

jess_support: Yep — grabbed from one of their failing nodes:
```
$ openssl s_client -connect api.acme.internal:443 -showcerts -servername api.acme.internal
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = Let'sEncrypt, CN = ISRG Root X1
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
Certificate chain
0 s:/CN=api.acme.internal
1 s:/C=US/O=ACME Co./CN=ACME Intermediate
---
```

ingrid_eng: Interesting — chain only shows leaf + one intermediate. Do we know if the LB/ingress is sending the full bundle? Could be missing the second intermediate.

jess_support: I also ran curl -v which fails with the same verify message on some pods and succeeds on others. Suspect client trust stores differ. But timeline lines up exactly with our rotation job that updated k8s secret.

arjun_sre: I pulled the ingress pod logs around rotation time — deploy-bot shows a secret apply event but no bundle concat step. Deploy logs: `kubectl apply -f acme-tls.yaml` then `deploy-bot: secret updated` — no verification step.

deploy-bot: automated-apply: secret acme-tls updated for ns=acme-prod

ingrid_eng: Do we have the script that builds the secret? I recall the rotation helper should append intermediates into `tls.crt` in leaf->intermediate->root order. If order is wrong some clients choke.

maria_security: Also check OCSP stapling — some clients rely on stapled responses and if egress to OCSP responder is blocked by customer allowlist the stapling may be empty and verify flows change. Are they blocking outbound traffic?

jess_support: Customer confirmed they have a restrictive egress allowlist. They only allow DNS and certain ports; OCSP (port 80 to letsencrypt.org) was not explicitly allowed.

tyler_oncall: That could explain why some JVM-based services (that prefer OCSP) fail while curl (which ignores stapling sometimes) works. Two hypotheses: (1) missing intermediate in chain, (2) OCSP blocked and stapling missing.

ingrid_eng: Quick checks we need from customer (one-liners):
- openssl s_client -connect api.acme.internal:443 -showcerts -servername api.acme.internal
- openssl s_client -connect api.acme.internal:443 -status -servername api.acme.internal (shows stapling)
- kubectl get secret acme-tls -n acme-prod -o yaml (we just need the tls.crt base64 blob)
- curl -v --cacert /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt https://api.acme.internal/health

jess_support: They ran the `-status` check — response says no OCSP response sent (no response received).

arjun_sre: OK. Action plan:
1) Ask customer to paste the decoded tls.crt from the secret. We'll verify the bundle order and presence of all intermediates.
2) If bundle missing intermediate, they should update secret with full chain (leaf + intermediate(s)). Provide them exact concat command.
3) If bundle correct, we check LB/ingress: sometimes envoy/nginx strips chain if configured incorrectly — collect `kubectl exec` into ingress and run `openssl s_client` to see what LB is serving.
4) Ask customer to open egress to OCSP responder (or allow our OCSP proxy) so stapling can work while we debug.

maria_security: Provide this command to re-bundle correctly:
```bash
cat leaf.crt intermediate.crt root.crt > fullchain.crt
kubectl create secret tls acme-tls --cert=fullchain.crt --key=leaf.key -n acme-prod --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
```
Note: order should be leaf -> intermediate(s) -> root (root optional but some stacks expect it).

jess_support: Customer pasted the decoded secret: only leaf + one intermediate, missing cross-signed intermediate that some clients expect.

tyler_oncall: That matches verify error. Inconsistent trust roots across internal services mean some rely on cross-signed intermediate chain. We need them to add the missing intermediate to secret and re-roll.

ingrid_eng: I'll open an eng-runtime ticket to add an automated verification step in our rotation playbook that fails if chain doesn't include expected intermediates (and optionally verify that LB serves fullchain).

maria_security: While they're updating allow them these mitigations:
- Re-upload fullchain including cross-signed intermediate.
- Temporarily allow outbound HTTP to ocsp.int-x3.letsencrypt.org (example) for OCSP queries.

jess_support: Customer is going to update secret now. I'll watch for a new deploy.

sre-bot: rollout detected: ingress/acme-ingress v2.1.5 -> v2.1.6 at 2023-11-27T15:05:12Z

arjun_sre: After they apply, please run `openssl s_client -connect api.acme.internal:443 -showcerts -servername api.acme.internal` from inside an affected pod and from the ingress to confirm both see the same chain.

jess_support: Update — they added the missing intermediate and re-applied. Initial checks look good from curl. JVM services still failing, but rebooting the pods picked up new trust path and two pods recovered. Remaining pod is an older JVM that caches certs aggressively; they're restarting it now.

tyler_oncall: Great. Follow-ups:
- eng-runtime to add chain verification in rotation job (ingrid to own).
- customer docs: add a note about egress to OCSP and testing commands (jess to update KB).
- eng-security to review whether we should POST-rotation run an active check against a standard client matrix (maria to own).

maria_security: I'll schedule a short RFC for making OCSP/responder tests part of our Private onboarding checklist.

jess_support: Closing loop with customer — they confirmed full recovery after final pod restarts. Will keep thread open for eng tickets. Thanks all :thumbsup:

ingrid_eng: Filed RUNTIME-427: rotation job: verify fullchain + serve-check.

maria_security: Filed SEC-312: private deployments OCSP allowlist guidance.

jess_support: Marking as resolved on support side; leaving eng tickets for follow-up. :white_check_mark:
